### Digital Publications and Projects
2026–present: *Markings/Huellas: Sensorial/Affect Map*. UCLA cityLAB, with community and institutional partners. Technical lead, Office of Advanced Research Computing, University of California, Los Angeles. An interactive mapping and oral-history platform documenting the experiences and place-making practices of Indigenous immigrant communities in Los Angeles, built by extending the open-source Terrastories platform so visitors can explore stories through cultural, thematic, and linguistic relationships as well as location. Includes a shared data model linking oral histories, narrators, places, and media. (In development)

2026–present: *CAL-DROP Statewide Program Dashboard*. For CAL-DROP (California Development and Rapid Operationalization of Prehospital Blood), a statewide coalition of 19 local EMS agencies, fire departments, hospitals, and blood banks establishing California's first ground EMS blood transfusion programs. Office of Advanced Research Computing, University of California, Los Angeles. Designer and developer. A prototype interactive Tableau dashboard integrating operational data from coalition partners across California, with statewide, county, and regional maps, time-based filters, and key performance indicators to support program evaluation and oversight, built on standardized partner data. Prototype delivered 2026; further development pending. <https://dhs.lacounty.gov/harbor-ucla-medical-center/work-or-partner-with-us/la-drop/>

2025: *Đại Nam Nhất Thống Chí (DNNTC) Viewer*. With George Dutton (Asian Languages and Cultures, UCLA). Office of Advanced Research Computing, University of California, Los Angeles. Designer and developer: data model, processing workflows, and web interface. An interactive viewer presenting the original woodblock text of all seventeen volumes alongside its transcription, with full-text search across more than 250,000 Classical Chinese characters, vertical right-to-left reading, and reader-submitted corrections. The largest known online Vietnamese historical text. (Forthcoming on Columbia University's Digitizing Vietnam platform)

2024–present: *Milken Archive of Jewish Music Wikibase*. For the Milken Archive of Jewish Music. Designer and developer. A reusable Python and Streamlit framework for transforming the archive's spreadsheet metadata into a linked-data knowledge graph in Wikibase, with FRBR-based modeling of works and expressions, entity reconciliation across datasets, configurable relationship mapping, and provenance-preserving statements. Designed to serve other digital humanities and cultural heritage datasets. (In development)

2023–2026: *Tracks of Yu: The Yellow River Database and Digital Atlas*. With Ruth Mostern and Nathan Michalewicz. Data coordinator and developer. The open database, documentation, and geodata behind Mostern's *The Yellow River: A Natural and Unnatural History* (Yale University Press, 2021), with a web atlas for exploring them. <https://tracksofyu.github.io/> Data and code: <https://github.com/TracksOfYu>

2021: *Yellow River: A Natural and Unnatural History*, by Ruth Mostern. Yale University Press. Maps and infographics.

2020–2022: *Sinai Manuscripts Digital Library*. Digital Library Program, UCLA Library. Data and metadata coordinator: site development and data and metadata development. <https://sinaimanuscripts.library.ucla.edu/>

2019–2020: *World Historical Gazetteer*. World History Center, University of Pittsburgh. Contributed to project and data model design; data coordination. <https://whgazetteer.org/>

2017–2022: *Black Lunch Table Audio Archive*. Black Lunch Table. Digital director: site and database design and development. <https://blacklunchtable.com/>

2017: *Hierokles' Synekdemos*. Ancient World Mapping Center, University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill. Site and database design and development. An interactive map of Hierokles' survey of the cities of the Eastern Roman Empire under Justinian. (Offline since 2023; AWMC released a redesigned version in 2026.) Archived: <https://web.archive.org/web/20220923174814/http://awmc.unc.edu/awmc/applications/hierokles/>

2017: *IAH Knowledge Network Map*. Institute for the Arts and Humanities, University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill. Site and database design and development. <https://iah-unc.github.io/knowledge-network/>

2017: *Asia Minor in the Second Century C.E.* With Richard Talbert, Brian Turner, Jeffrey Becker, Ross Twele, and Gabriel Moss. Ancient World Mapping Center, University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill. Cartographer and data coordinator. A 1:750,000 wall map succeeding J. G. C. Anderson's 1903 map of the region. <https://awmc.unc.edu/wall-maps/>

2015: *Strabo Digital Mapping Application*. Ancient World Mapping Center, University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill, accompanying Duane W. Roller, *The Geography of Strabo: An English Translation, with Introduction and Notes* (Cambridge University Press, 2014). Designer and developer. (Offline since 2023; AWMC released a redesigned version in 2026.) Archived: <https://web.archive.org/web/20231128110529/http://www.awmc.unc.edu/awmc/applications/strabo/>

2015: *Terra Biblica and BAM (Big Ancient Mediterranean) Online Resources*. With Sarah Bond and Paul Dilley. University of Iowa. Designer and developer. <http://bam.lib.uiowa.edu/>

2014: *AWMC Map Tiles*. Ancient World Mapping Center, University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill. Cartographer, designer, and developer. Geographically accurate, publicly accessible map tiles of the ancient world for use in web maps, which received over 2.5 million views a year. (Offline.) Archived: <https://web.archive.org/web/20231127020205/http://awmc.unc.edu/wordpress/tiles/>

2012–present: *Pleiades*. Ancient World Mapping Center and Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, New York University. Contributor and editor. A peer-reviewed, community-built gazetteer and graph of ancient places. <https://pleiades.stoa.org/>

2012: *Antiquity À-la-carte*. Ancient World Mapping Center, University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill. Creator and programmer. A web-based GIS and interactive digital atlas of the ancient world. (Offline.) Archived: <https://web.archive.org/web/20231127020207/http://awmc.unc.edu/wordpress/alacarte/>

2011: *Peutinger Map*. Digital map accompanying Richard J. A. Talbert, *Rome's World: The Peutinger Map Reconsidered* (Cambridge University Press, 2010), with Tom Elliott, Nora Harris, and Martin Steinmann. Developer. (Offline.) Archived: <https://web.archive.org/web/20250409170428/https://peutinger.atlantides.org/map-a/>
